title: Objects and Materials
seo_title: Year 1 Science: Objects and Materials Worksheets (Wood, Metal, Plastic, Glass)
standard_text: Distinguish between an object and the material from which it is made. Identify and name a variety of everyday materials, including wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, and rock.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 science worksheets on objects and materials: telling an object from its material, naming wood, plastic, glass, metal, water and rock, and sorting objects. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A spoon is an object; metal is its material.
body_html:
How to think about it

Objects are made of materials.

  • A spoon is an object. Metal is its material.
  • Wood, metal, glass, plastic, rock and water are materials.
  • One kind of object can be made of different materials.
Example

Spoon: object or material?

It is a thing

Answer: an object

Example

A window is made of?

See-through

Answer: glass

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a chair is a material.
  • Thinking glass and plastic are the same.
  • Thinking an object can only be made of one material.

faq.q: What is the difference between an object and a material?
faq.a: An object is a thing, like a spoon or a chair. A material is what it is made of, like metal or wood.

faq.q: What everyday materials should Year 1 know?
faq.a: Wood, plastic, glass, metal, water and rock, and also fabric, paper and rubber.

faq.q: Can one object be made of different materials?
faq.a: Yes. A spoon can be metal, plastic or wood, and a pencil uses wood, graphite and rubber.
